title: Case: Perishable delivery delayed by carrier network alert
context: A food delivery is held up during a carrier-wide system outage affecting tracking and dispatch allocation. The consignee has a time-sensitive product. The desk must communicate honestly about known delays without inventing recovery timelines.
initial_request: Coordinate response to consignee concern about a delayed perishable shipment during a network incident.

events.body: Network alert issued 08:00 UTC: tracking database offline, all dispatch assignments frozen pending restoration. Estimated restoration 2-4 hours. All shipments in transit or pending collection are held. DL-987 and 340 others affected.
Where is my delivery DL-987? It should be here by 09:30. I have live crickets for my bearded dragon and they have to go in the vivarium this morning or they'll die. This is urgent.
Still nothing. The crickets are in a box with 8 hours air and it's already been 9 hours since I ordered. Can you tell me when the driver is coming or do I need to go buy different food elsewhere?

acceptable_actions.summary: Acknowledge the time-sensitive issue, explain the network outage affecting his shipment and many others, commit to update when tracking restores without guaranteeing a time.

must: State honestly that a carrier network outage is delaying DL-987 and other shipments.
Do not invent or promise a specific delivery window or time.
Do not treat this as a one-off investigation case or suggest the shipment will be prioritised over the network-wide issue.
must_not: Promise delivery 'within 2 hours' or any other time based on the carrier's estimate.
Apologise for the crickets dying or accept liability for the delay.
Suggest Marcus open a damage claim or contact the merchant yet.
Say the shipment is lost or may not arrive today.
expected.reference_message: Hi Marcus, thank you for the alert. Your shipment DL-987 is held up in a carrier network outage that started at 08:00 UTC and affects over 300 shipments. Tracking is offline and dispatch is frozen. We're waiting for Plover Arc to restore their systems. Once they do, we'll have a clearer picture of where your delivery sits in the queue. I'll update you as soon as I hear more. Sorry for the stress with the crickets.

rationale: The desk must be honest that a known network event is the cause, not a mystery or rare failure. Giving false timelines to a consignee with a genuinely time-sensitive product damages trust and invites complaints when the optimistic estimate fails. This is not a one-off investigation case; it is a known, widespread incident. The desk contacts the consignee with the facts and a realistic promise to update, nothing more.
